ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Global Korean Diasporas Colonialism, war, and national division have resulted in substantial communities of ethnic Koreans in Central Asia, China, Japan, and the United States, as well as Canada, South America, and Europe. By examining the histories of ethnic Koreans in these places, we will explore issues of migration, diaspora, race, policies regarding minorities, and colonialism. We will also take a fresh look at 20th century Korean history, demonstrating how diaspora and emigration are critical to understanding national history. This class will be offered online via Big Ten Academic Alliance CourseShare (Northwestern University, taught by Prof. Ji-Yeon Yuh) and will be taught synchronously utilizing Zoom.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Not intended for students with Junior or Senior class standing.
